correctness.rationale: Differentiate the bounded-past exponential convolution to m_dot=lambda(x-m); orthogonal Laplacian diagonalization gives p_u(z)=z^2+(lambda+a*u)z+lambda*u*(a+b). Both coefficients of p_u(z-r) are affine in u; the closed-left-half-plane Hurwitz criterion yields the exact extremal-mode bound between alpha and beta for all intermediate modes. A one-mode discriminant and monotonic-rate analysis places the unique alpha/beta crossing strictly between their critical gains; the positive quadratic root gives a*. At a* and alpha<beta the two endpoint roots are nondefective, so the rate is attained; alpha=beta gives a Jordan t*exp(-R*t) and only the supremum. A bounded continuous past can realize each modal (X0,M0), so sharpness is observable in x. Independently checked 2,500 parameter tuples and interior-mode rates. These samples support, not substitute, the affine Hurwitz argument.
